:J U D G M E N T:
This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 12.11.2018.
2.

The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 12.11.2018 at about 10.30 a.m., the petitioner was standing near Ijoor circle,
opposite to Bairaveshwara medical shop, Bangalore-Mysore road, Ramanagara Town, Ramanagara District by observing all vehicular movements on the extreme side of the mud road.

At that point of time, the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-R-7008 ridden from Bangalore side towards Mysore side with high speed in a rash or negligent manner without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the petitioner. Due to impact, petitioner sustained severe injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital,
Ramanagara, after first aid he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital, Bangalore and then he was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Hospital, Bangalore, wherein the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient.

Thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to Narayana Hospital, Ramanagara, wherein also the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient,
X-rays, CT Scan and MRI Scans were taken and the petitioner was undergone conservative effective treatment and he was discharged with an advise to take regular follow-up treatment and bed rest.
The petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, nourishment and attendant charges.

The injuries sustained by the petitioner were not united and he has undergone severe pain often, he cannot stand or squat, carry any weight, suffered with head ache,
double vision, disfigurement and he has suffered permanent disability.

The petitioner was aged 40 years at the time of accident and he was earing a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month by doing electrician work, assistance work, contract work on temporary basis at Water Supply Board, Kanakapura Town.

The petitioner has maintained his family out of his income and due to accidental injuries, he could not attend his work permanently, which resulted loss of earning and put him to great financial hardship.
The accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-R- 7008 and after investigation, the Ramanagara police have Purushotham Rao vs Divyashree.R

2 filed charge sheet against the rider of aforesaid motor cycle for the offence punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC.
The 1st respondent being the RC owner of motor cycle bewaring Reg.No.KA-42-R-7008 and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of the said vehicle and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
3. After service of notice, 1st respondent-R.C. owenr of offending vehcile and 2nd respondent-Insurance company appeared through their counsel and filed written statements.

4. The written statement averments of the 1st respondent are hereunder:
The 1st respondent has denied the profession and income of the petitioner, injuries sustained, treatment taken and amount spend by the petitioner.
She has admitted that, she is the RC owner of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-R-7008 and the said vehicle was insured with the 2nd respondent.

The 1st respondent has contended that,
the rider of offending vehicle riding the same in a normal speed with extra caution and he never ride the vehicle with high speed and dashed against the petitioner.
The accident was not occurred due to negligence on the part of the rider of offending vehicle, which is due to only on the part of petitioner.
The police have filed false case against the rider of motor cycle.
It is contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant and without any basis.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. The written statement averments of the 2nd respondent are hereunder:
This respondent has admitting the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-R-7008, interalia contended that, the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy, valid D.L. held by the rider of offending vehicle, R.C. and F.C. of said vehicle.
The rider of aforesaid motor cycle was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
It is clear violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

The 1st respondent has violated the mandatory provisions under Sec.134(c) of M.V. Act and the police have also violatged provisions under Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act by not sending the vehicular documents to the 2nd respondent.
The accident was occurred due to negligence of the petitioner, who was walking on the middle of the road by violating the traffic ruels.
The 2 nd respondent has denied the injuries sustained, treatment taken, amount spent and permanently disability sustianed by the petitioner.
Further denied the profession and income of the petitioner.
It is contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following :ISSUES:

The findings of this Tribunal to the above referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 :- In the Partly Affirmative.

Issue No.3 :- As per the final order, for the following:

ISSUE No.1:-
In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7.

Accordingly,
Ex.P.1 is the true copy of FIR pertaining to Cr.No.165/2018.
Ex.P.2 is the true copy of Complaint.
Ex.P.3 is the true copy of spot mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is the true copy of spot sketch.
Ex.P.5 is the true copy of M.V.A. Report.
Ex.P.6 is the true copy of wound certificate.
Ex.P.7 is the true copy of charge sheet.

10. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

11. According to the petitioner, he has sustained injuries in the road accident.

According to the respondent Nos.1 and 2, the accident was occurred due to negligence of the petitioner who was walking on the middle of the road by violating the traffic rules at the time fo accident.
In order to substantiate the same, Insurance company has not placed positive evidence.

Likewise, insurance Purushotham Rao vs Divyashree.R on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139751684/
4 company-2nd respondent neither examined the rider of offending vehicle nor ocular witnesses to the incident to establish its defence.
12. Further, to prove the alleged negligence on the part of petitioner, the Insurance Company has cross- examined the petitioner/P.W.1 in detail.
Nothing has been elicited from mouth of P.W.1 to establish that the accident was took place only on the negligence of petitioner.
At the cost of repetition, to substantiate it6 pts contention, Insurance company has not placed positive evidence.

At this juncture it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka between National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Krishnappa and Another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, "the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scootrist".

sentences.text: In the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.2, complaint was lodged before Ramanagara Traffic Police Station.
Thereafter, as per Ex.P.1, FIR was lodged against the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-KA-42-R-7008.

On careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.7, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the ridder of the offending vehicle and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.7 after completing investigation.

A careful perusal of Ex.P.6, it clearly goes to show that,
the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

Further, on perusal of Ex.P.7 i.e.,
charge sheet, it reveals that, the rider of offending vehicle i.e., Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-R-7008 has been arrayed as an accused.

14. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the petitioner was crossing the road, the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-R-7008 came in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
The evidence placed on record is clearly reveals that rider of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-R-7008 has caused the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE No.2:-
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the accident was caused due to the rash or negligent riding of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 42-R-7008.
It is needless to mention that, 1st respondent is the R.C. owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
According to the petitioner, he was aged 40 years as on the date of accident.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.15 viz., the notarized copy of his Aadhaar Card.
On perusal of this document it appears to this Tribunal that, the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 01.01.1970.
The accident was occurred on 12.11.2018.
Accordingly, the age of the petitioner is considered as 48 years.
17. Income:-

In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he was doing electrician work, apart from that he was doing assistant work on contract basis at Water Supply Board, Kanakapura Town and he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Per-contra, the 2 nd respondent has denied the income of petitioner.
To substantiate the income of petitioner, he has not placed any documentary evidence.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in Purushotham Rao vs Divyashree.R on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139751684/
5 M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another,

" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".

18. In the absence of reliable document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the petitioner is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2018 is Rs.12,500/- per month.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 12.11.2018.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.12,500/-
per month.

19. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-
(Income X year X Multiplier X Disability)

In the instant case, the petitioner has stated in his affidavit that, he has sustained injury measuring 2X1 cm., over occipital region, swelling over occipital region, abrasion over lower end of laceratin spain measuring 2X1, fracture of lateral wall of left maxillary sinus and linear fracture of left mastoid bone and mandibular fossa.
In order to substantiate the same, he has relied on Ex.P.6 i.e., wound certificate and Ex.P.11 i.e., discharge summary and Ex.P.12 i.e., C.T. Scan Report.

On perusal of Ex.P.12 it reveal that, the petitioner has sustained fracture of lateral wall of left maxillary sinus, linear fracture of left mastoid bone and mandibular fossa, linear fracture of occipital bone and left periorbital and temporal region soft tissue swelling.
It is relevant to mention that, respondent No.2 has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1.
P.W.1 also stated that, the injuries sustained in the accident have not united and getting unbearable pain often.

Further stated that, he cannot carry weight, he has suffered partial head ache, double vision,
cannot take smell, suffered breathing problem, disfigurement and cannot do any work and also suffered permanent disability.

20. In order to prove the physical disability/injuries, the petitioner examined medical witness namely Dr.Shailesh A.V. Rao, Senior Consultant Neurosurgeon at Padmashree Diagnostics,
Vijayanagara, Bengaluru as P.W.2.
This witness has filed the affidavit in lieu of evidence and stated that he has examined the petitioner on 08.09.2023 and 09.09.2023 for the assessment of disability.
He has stated that, left temporal bone fracture, pneumocephalus, ethmoid fracture, fracture of left maxilla, left mastoid and left occipital bone.
Further stated that, petitioner could not able to attend his earlier work as a manual labourer.
The petitioner complains impaired memory, impaired intelligence, frequent headaches, frequent giddiness.
On examination, it reveals that, the petitioner is a conscious patient with impaired memory and intelligence and also he is talking irrelevantly and Purushotham Rao vs Divyashree.

Further learned counsel for the petitioner argued that, if the permanent disabiltiy if more than 30%,

sentences.text: In the instant case, the petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 by filing affidavit.
Thereafter, he was subject to the process of cross-examination.
During the course of his cross-examination, he has denied the suggestion that, there was no negligence on the part of rider of the two wheeler.

By careful perusal of the entire cross-examination of P.W.1, it can be inferred that, P.W.1 deposed before this Tribunal without any loss of memore or neuropsychological disorder as stated in the petition.
Further it can be inferred that, the petitioner has conscious while deposing before this Tribunal.
Apart from that, P.W.2 admitted that, on 08.09.2023 and 09.09.2023, he was assessed the petitioner.
He was examined the petitioner on 22.03.2021 and he was cross-examined on 07.08.2021.
Therefore, it is crystal clear that, subsequent to the evidence of P.W.1, P.W.2 has assessed the disability of P.W.1.
As such, this Tribunal is declained to consider the entire evidence of P.w.2.
Apart from that, the petitioner was treated conservatively.
Under such circumstances, this Tribunal consider the disability of the petitioner at 12% to the whole body.
Under such circumstances, the decision relied by the petitioner will not come to the aid of petitioner since the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a factually distinguishable case.
23. As discussed supra, age of the injured is considered as 48 years and his income is considered as Rs.12,500/- per month.
Annual income comes to Rs.1,50,000/-(12,500 x 12).
Hence, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of injured as per Sarala Verma case is 13.
If we multiplied yearly income with proper multiplier (1,50,000X 13), then it comes to Rs.19,50,000/-.
Already this Tribunal has considered the disability of petitioner as 12% to the whole body.
The same amount of Rs.2,34,000/- is awarded to the Injured/Petitioner under the head of loss of Future Income due to disabiltiy.

Medical Expenses:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, nourishment and attendant charges.
In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced 17 medical bills marked as Ex.P.13 for Rs.21,326/- and 14 medical prescriptions marked as Ex.P.14.
This Tribunal has carefully perused the medical bills and found same are correct.
Apart from that, there is no serious dispute regarding authencity of medical bills.
After careful perusal of the medical bills, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for Rs.21,326/-, towards medical expenses.
25. Pain and suffering:-
According to the petitioner, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Ramanagara Government Hospital, after first aid he was shifted to NIMHANS Hospital.
Then the petitioner was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Hospital, Bengaluru for futher management.
Thereafter he was shifted to Narayana Hospital, Ramanagara, wherein he has taken treatmetn as an inpatient from 12.11.2018 to 16.11.2018.

P.W.1 stated that, the injuries sustained in the accident are not united, he is getting unbearable pain often, he could not walk or stand, carry any weight, he is suffering partial head ache, double vision and cannot take smell, facing breathing problem,
disfigurement and he cannot do his routine work.
As per Ex.P.8, Ex.P.9, Ex.P.10 the petitioner has sustained head injury and taken treatment.
Ex . P.11
, the Discharge summary reveals that, the petitioner was admitted at Narayana Hospital, Ramanagara as an inpatient for a period of 5 days i.e., from 12.11.2018 to 16.11.2018.
As per Ex.P.7, i.e., discharge summary coupled with evidence of P.W.2, it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained head injury.
There is no serious dispute with regard to inpatient for five days.
As such, the petitioner suffered a lot of pain and inconvenience.

Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal grants compensation of Rs.20,000/-
under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

26. Loss of income during the laidup period:-
The petitioner has produced discharge summary and same has been marked as Ex.
On perusal of this document, it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for five days.
However, the petitioner has not produced documents to show that, how many days he has taken bed rest.
Naturally it shows that, he might have taken atleast one month rest because of the injuries.
He has averred that, he was doing electrician work and assistance work on contract basis at Water Supply Board, Kanakapura Town and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But he has not produced documents to substantiate the same.
Hence, this Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.12,500/- per month.
Hence, two months is to be considered as loss of income during laidup period.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.12,500/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
27. Food, Nourishment and Atttendant charges:-
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatinet for about five days.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents in this regard.

Hence,

28. Loss of future amenities and happiness:-
The petitioner was aged about 49 years at the time of accident.
As per Ex.P.11, i.e., discharge summary coupled with evidence of P.W.2, it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained head injury.
Though the fractures are united, the petitioner has sustained pain because of said injuries.
Therefore, the petitioner has to live with the said disability for the rest of his life.
Therefore, he might have suffered pain, discomforts in life and loss of amenities.
By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disabiltiy, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.

Regarding liability and interest.
According to respondsent No.2, the rider of offending vehicle was not holding valid driving licence to drive the vehicle.
Learned counsel for the 2 nd respondent would submit that driver of offending vehicle had no driving license at the time of accident.
Further, learned counsel for 2nd Respondent in his written arguments submitted that the 1st Respondent is the owner of the vehicle.
The 1 st Respondent knowingly handed over the vehicle to a person who was not knowing the driving and also not having driving license to ride the motor cycle.
Hence, liability cannot be fastened upon the 2nd Respondent-Insurance company and prayed to dismiss the petition against 2nd Respondent.

33. This Tribunal has carefully perused the decision relied by the petitioner.

On meticulous reading of the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka (Division Bench), it appers to this Tribunal that, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka after discussing the several judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court rendered in National Insurance Co., Vs. Swarna Singh and Others, Shamanna and Another Vs. Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Co., and Others, Pappu and Others Vs., Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another and full bench decission of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A.
No.30131/2021 dated: 12.05.2020 between New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Yallavva and Others held that, "the charge sheet has been filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: In the circumstances, applying the principles of law has held in the judgments referred (Supra) "pay and recover" is to be ordered.
It is to be held that, the owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.

As the offending vehicle was duly covered by the policy issued by the insurer as on the date of accident, the insurer shall satisfy the award to the claimant in the first instance and is at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle".
34.
The first decision relied by the 2 nd respondent and the decision relied by the petitioner are the decisions of Division Bench.
It is pivotal to note that, subordinate Courts are governed under Article 141 of Indian Constitution which deals with law of precedents.
The decision relied by the 2nd respondent is rendered by the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka on 13.04.2023.
However, the decision relied by the counsel for the petitioner is rendered by the Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka on 25.04.2024.

:J U D G M E N T:
This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 12.11.2018.
2.
opennyai_summary.facts:
The 1st respondent being the RC owner of motor cycle bewaring Reg.No.KA-42-R-7008 and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of the said vehicle and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence, both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The 1st respondent has contended that,
the rider of offending vehicle riding the same in a normal speed with extra caution and he never ride the vehicle with high speed and dashed against the petitioner.
The accident was not occurred due to negligence on the part of the rider of offending vehicle, which is due to only on the part of petitioner.
The police have filed false case against the rider of motor cycle.
The 1st respondent has violated the mandatory provisions under Sec.134(c) of M.V. Act and the police have also violatged provisions under Sec.158(6) of M.V. Act by not sending the vehicular documents to the 2nd respondent.
The accident was occurred due to negligence of the petitioner, who was walking on the middle of the road by violating the traffic ruels.
The 2 nd respondent has denied the injuries sustained, treatment taken, amount spent and permanently disability sustianed by the petitioner.
Further denied the profession and income of the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The rider of aforesaid motor cycle was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
It is clear violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Thereafter, he was subject to the process of cross-examination.
opennyai_summary.issue:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries on account of rash and negligent driving of Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-42-R-7008 by its driver as contended in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he is entitled for the compensation?
If so, to what extent and from whom?
3. What order or award?
